newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil orange crop matures early after heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Brazil orange crop matures early after heavy rains.

text.p: Hot weather and heavy rains in May and June have helped Brazil's 1996/97 orange crop mature earlier than expected and prompted the premature flowering of next year's crop, growers said.
"It was probably the excess rain," said Leonardo Kossoy, president of the Association of Citrus Growers of Sao Paulo State (Aciesp). "It rained mainly in May and June, which are usually dry months."
"Quality is very good, the oranges are very juicy because of the rains," he added.

Yields for the early Hamlin variety were averaging 240 boxes of fruit per tonne of frozen concentrated orange juice while for the midseason Pera variety some plants reached yields of 190 boxes per tonne, a private analyst said.
However, the oranges looked uglier because producers had not invested in spraying crops, growers said.
Producers were being paid between $2.50 and $2.80 per 40.8 kg box, while growers who did not have contracts with producers were receiving $2.12 to $2.20 per box, Kossoy said.
Growers will have to pace harvesting of the bumper 1996/97 crop, forecast at 405 million boxes, and processors may have to extend their operations this year, he said.

"At the present pace of harvesting and processing it appears that most processors will be finished crushing this season's crop around Christmas with very little fruit expected to be available in January," said the private analyst.

The early flowering of the 1997/98 crop was likely to result in two harvests, but this would not necessarily mean double the crop and some growers were concerned about the extra cost of harvesting in two stages.
"The plants end up flowering twice, once now and once at the normal time, which means two harvests and twice as many costs," said Kossoy.
